## Overview

PBMCs from two independent 10x runs (PBMC5k and PBMC10k, `{{input.n_batches}}` batches under obs column `{{input.batch_key}}`) were combined into one object of `{{input.n_cells}}` cells x `{{input.n_genes}}` genes and taken from raw counts to annotated cell types. Because the two runs are a technical grouping rather than a biological condition, batch correction was used purely to align cell types for clustering/annotation, while raw counts were preserved throughout.

## Quality control

Gene identifiers were confirmed as human gene symbols with a `MT-` mitochondrial prefix (`{{qc.n_mito_genes}}` mitochondrial genes detected), so mitochondrial QC metrics are reliable.

The mitochondrial fraction in this dataset runs noticeably higher than a typical tutorial PBMC sample: median `{{qc.mito.median}}`, p75 `{{qc.mito.p75}}`, p95 `{{qc.mito.p95}}`, max `{{qc.mito.max}}`. Applying the tutorial-default cap of `{{default.max_pct_mt}}` would have discarded `{{default.mito_cells_removed}}` cells (`{{default.mito_pct_removed}}` of the dataset) — clearly excessive and indicative of a shifted baseline rather than widespread cell damage. I instead used a permissive cap of `{{filter.max_pct_mt}}`, which trims only the true high-mito tail (roughly the top 2-3%) while keeping the bulk of the biologically real population. The gene-count floor (`{{filter.min_genes}}`) removed no cells on its own, since the empirical minimum (`{{qc.genes.min}}` genes/cell) already exceeds it — this dataset had no very-low-complexity droplets to begin with. Combined cell filtering removed `{{filter.cells_removed}}` cells (`{{filter.pct_cells_removed}}`), and the gene floor (`{{filter.min_cells}}` cells/gene) removed `{{filter.genes_removed}}} `lowly-detected genes.

## Doublet detection

Scrublet was run separately within each 10x run (`{{doublet.distribution}}` overall, i.e. no clean bimodal valley to split on). Following the standard rule for data without prior doublet removal, I used median + 3xMAD (`{{doublet.threshold}}`), which sits well below either run's Scrublet automatic threshold (`{{doublet.scrublet_auto}}`) and flags a plausible `{{doublet.pct_removed}}` of cells as doublets — in line with expected multiplet rates for standard (non-hashed, non-demultiplexed) 10x loading. This removed `{{doublet.cells_removed}}` cells, leaving `{{doublet.cells_after}}`.

## Dimensionality reduction

The two 10x runs are a genuine technical batch (separate captures/libraries), so I used scVI (batch key = `{{input.batch_key}}`, `{{scvi.n_latent}}`-dim latent space, `{{scvi.epochs}}` epochs) rather than plain PCA. This lets clustering and UMAP reflect shared cell-type structure across runs instead of run-of-origin, while leaving raw counts untouched for any downstream expression analysis.

## Clustering

Leiden clustering on the scVI embedding (resolution `{{cluster.resolution}}`) yielded `{{cluster.n}}` clusters, ranging from `{{cluster.smallest}}` to `{{cluster.largest}}` cells (see cluster table).

{{table:clusters}}

## Cell-type annotation

CellTypist (Immune_All_Low.pkl, majority-voted per cluster) was used for initial labels, cross-checked against the coarser Immune_All_High.pkl model and canonical markers verified with `check_markers`.

- **Classical monocytes** (clusters 0, 1): high {{gene:Classical monocytes:CD14}}-consistent signal and {{gene:Classical monocytes:LYZ}}/{{gene:Classical monocytes:FCN1}} enrichment, S100A8/A9/A12 program; both models agree (monocyte at broad level).
- **Non-classical monocytes** (cluster 11): {{gene:Non-classical monocytes:FCGR3A}} and {{gene:Non-classical monocytes:MS4A7}} strongly enriched, CD14 not enriched — the classic CD16+ monocyte profile, distinct from clusters 0/1.
- **CD16+ NK cells** (cluster 2): {{gene:CD16+ NK cells:GNLY}}, {{gene:CD16+ NK cells:NKG7}} and {{gene:CD16+ NK cells:FCGR3A}} all top-ranked and highly enriched, CD3 absent.
- **Naive B cells** (cluster 3): {{gene:Naive B cells:CD79A}} and {{gene:Naive B cells:MS4A1}} essentially exclusive to this cluster.
- **DC2** (cluster 6): {{gene:DC2:FCER1A}} and {{gene:DC2:CD1C}} both highly specific and enriched, with HLA-DR genes co-expressed.
- **pDC** (cluster 12): {{gene:pDC:IL3RA}} and {{gene:pDC:CLEC4C}} essentially unique to this cluster (top-ranked, 95-100% expressing).
- **Tcm/Naive helper T cells** (cluster 4) and **Tem/Effector helper T cells** (cluster 7): both {{gene:Tcm/Naive helper T cells:CD3D}}/{{gene:Tcm/Naive helper T cells:CD3E}} and {{gene:Tem/Effector helper T cells:CD3D}}/{{gene:Tem/Effector helper T cells:CD3E}} strongly enriched with high {{gene:Tcm/Naive helper T cells:IL7R}}/{{gene:Tem/Effector helper T cells:IL7R}}, CD8A/B negative — CD4 T cells at two activation/differentiation states (cluster 4's top markers being dominated by ribosomal genes is consistent with the smaller transcriptome typical of resting/naive T cells).
- **Tcm/Naive cytotoxic T cells** (cluster 5) and **Tem/Trm cytotoxic T cells** (cluster 9): both CD3-positive with {{gene:Tcm/Naive cytotoxic T cells:CD8A}}/{{gene:Tcm/Naive cytotoxic T cells:CD8B}} and {{gene:Tem/Trm cytotoxic T cells:CD8A}}/{{gene:Tem/Trm cytotoxic T cells:CD8B}} enriched; cluster 9 additionally carries {{gene:Tem/Trm cytotoxic T cells:CCL5}} and {{gene:Tem/Trm cytotoxic T cells:GZMK}}, marking an effector/memory phenotype versus cluster 5's naive/central-memory profile.
- **MAIT cells** (cluster 10): {{gene:MAIT cells:KLRB1}} in essentially all cells of the cluster, with co-expressed {{gene:MAIT cells:GZMK}} and {{gene:MAIT cells:IL7R}}, matching the semi-invariant MAIT signature.
- **Low-quality/stressed cells** (cluster 8, relabeled): CellTypist's second-opinion label of "T cells" was not supported — {{gene:Low-quality/stressed cells:CD3D}} and {{gene:Low-quality/stressed cells:CD3E}} were not significantly enriched (expression indistinguishable from the rest of the dataset), nor were CD14, MS4A1 or NKG7. Instead its defining markers were {{gene:Low-quality/stressed cells:MALAT1}} and {{gene:Low-quality/stressed cells:MT-CO1}} alongside immediate-early genes (JUN, FOSB, IER2) — a stress/dissociation artifact signature rather than a lineage, so it was relabeled and should be treated as background rather than a real cell type in any downstream use of this dataset.

{{table:composition}}

Final annotated dataset: `{{final.n_cells}}` cells across `{{celltype.n}}` labels, dominated by {{celltype:Classical monocytes}} classical monocytes and {{celltype:Tcm/Naive helper T cells}} naive/central-memory CD4 T cells, with smaller but clearly resolved populations of DCs (`{{celltype:DC2}}` DC2, `{{celltype:pDC}}` pDC) and the small stressed-cell cluster (`{{celltype:Low-quality/stressed cells}}` cells).

## Caveats

- The mitochondrial threshold (`{{filter.max_pct_mt}}`) was chosen specifically for this dataset's shifted mito distribution; it is more permissive than the usual tutorial default and should not be reused unexamined on other data.
- Doublet removal used a global median+3MAD threshold per the standard rule; a small number of borderline cells near the cutoff are inherently ambiguous, and true heterotypic doublets between transcriptionally similar clusters (e.g. the two CD4 T-cell states) may be under-detected.
- Cluster 8 ("Low-quality/stressed cells", `{{celltype:Low-quality/stressed cells}}` cells) shows no coherent marker program and should be excluded from any biological interpretation; it likely reflects a small population of stressed/damaged cells that passed the permissive mito filter.
- scVI batch correction (on `{{input.batch_key}}`) was used to align cell types across the two 10x runs for clustering; this changes only the embedding used for neighbors/UMAP/clustering, not the raw counts, but any subtle run-specific biological differences could in principle be partially smoothed by the correction.

## Conclusions

Standard PBMC lineages were recovered cleanly after batch-aware integration of the two 10x runs: classical and non-classical monocytes, CD16+ NK cells, naive B cells, DC2 and pDC dendritic subsets, and CD4/CD8 T cells spanning naive/central-memory and effector/memory states plus MAIT cells. Every retained label is supported by canonical, statistically enriched markers verified directly against the ranked marker tables; the one CellTypist call not supported by markers (cluster 8) was identified as a stress artifact and relabeled accordingly.
